citations.finding: Trauma exposures differed between countries; reported PTSD prevalence did not differ significantly.
citations.fullCitation: Corneil W, Beaton R, Murphy S, Johnson C, Pike K. Exposure to traumatic incidents and prevalence of posttraumatic stress symptomatology in urban firefighters in two countries. Journal of Occupational Health Psychology. 1999;4(2):131-141.
citations.limitations: Cross-sectional, self-report; contextual and individual differences.
citations.pendingReview: Full text and formal bias appraisal pending
citations.supportedUse: Supports event and context documentation, not a universal event-to-symptom dose curve.

citations.finding: Individual factors and social support were associated with differences in posttraumatic and depressive symptoms.
citations.fullCitation: Regehr C, Hill J, Glancy GD. Individual predictors of traumatic reactions in firefighters. The Journal of Nervous and Mental Disease. 2000;188(6):333-339.
citations.limitations: No validation of entrapment trigger or event weights; no personality profiling.
citations.pendingReview: Full text and formal bias appraisal pending
citations.supportedUse: Supports keeping incident facts separate from individual response.

citations.finding: Emotional connection with patients or families was associated with greater reported traumatic stress.
citations.fullCitation: Regehr C, Goldberg G, Hughes J. Exposure to human tragedy, empathy, and trauma in ambulance paramedics. The American Journal of Orthopsychiatry. 2002;72(4):505-513.
citations.limitations: Does not establish that every pediatric emergency meets Criterion A or diagnose a responder.
citations.pendingReview: Full text and formal bias appraisal pending
citations.supportedUse: Context for pediatric and close-person review flags.

citations.finding: Pooled current PTSD prevalence was 10%; estimates varied across populations.
citations.fullCitation: Berger W, Coutinho ES, Figueira I, Marques-Portella C, Luz MP, Neylan TC, Marmar CR, Mendlowicz MV. Rescuers at risk: a systematic review and meta-regression analysis of the worldwide current prevalence and correlates of PTSD in rescue workers. Social Psychiatry and Psychiatric Epidemiology. 2012;47(6):1001-1011.
citations.limitations: Current prevalence is not individual probability; overlapping studies with later reviews.
citations.pendingReview: Full text and formal bias appraisal pending
citations.supportedUse: Background rationale for research and support access.

citations.finding: Reviewed work-related PTSD and contextual factors including social support and prior mental health.
citations.fullCitation: Skogstad M, Skorstad M, Lie A, Conradi HS, Heir T, Weisaeth L. Work-related post-traumatic stress disorder. Occupational Medicine (Oxford, England). 2013;63(3):175-182.
citations.limitations: Does not validate a fixed half-life, automatic dispatch classification or symptom inference.
citations.pendingReview: Full text and formal bias appraisal pending
citations.supportedUse: Occupational context; supports separate clinical and event layers.

citations.finding: Remains handlers reported more intrusive and avoidant symptoms; experience modified findings.
citations.fullCitation: McCarroll JE, Ursano RJ, Fullerton CS. Symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder following recovery of war dead. The American Journal of Psychiatry. 1993;150(12):1875-1877.
citations.limitations: Military war-dead setting; not a validated civilian firefighter coefficient.
citations.pendingReview: Full text and formal bias appraisal pending
citations.supportedUse: Context for documenting occupational contact with human remains.

citations.finding: Describes exposure routes and the additional symptom, duration, impairment and exclusion criteria.
citations.fullCitation: US Department of Veterans Affairs, National Center for PTSD. PTSD and DSM-5.
citations.limitations: Incident flags alone cannot establish a personal Criterion A route or PTSD.

citations.finding: Describes a 20-item self-report assessment and clinician interpretation; screening is not a dispatch-derived diagnosis.
citations.fullCitation: US Department of Veterans Affairs, National Center for PTSD. PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5).
citations.limitations: No questionnaire values, cutoff flags or inferred symptoms in shared incident or unit records.

classes.exclusionBoundary: A Mayday opens a review. It does not establish that anything happened.
classes.label: A member killed or seriously hurt
classes.requiredCorroboration: A death or serious injury, plus evidence of who witnessed it.

classes.exclusionBoundary: A collapse or a flashover somewhere on the fireground does not establish exposure for everyone who responded.
classes.label: A member trapped or out of air
classes.requiredCorroboration: Entrapment, loss of air or an immediate life threat to the affected person.

classes.exclusionBoundary: A pediatric dispatch, a transport priority or an age on its own is not enough.
classes.label: A child killed or critically hurt
classes.requiredCorroboration: A corroborated event, and relevant in person witnessing.

classes.exclusionBoundary: A death, an unsuccessful resuscitation or an expected natural death does not on its own establish the exposure route.
classes.label: A civilian death
classes.requiredCorroboration: Corroborated traumatic circumstances, and an actual witnessing route reviewed.

classes.exclusionBoundary: A mass casualty dispatch or a staging assignment on its own is not enough.
classes.label: Multiple casualties at one incident
classes.requiredCorroboration: Confirmed casualties and responder contact, with the count uncertainty preserved.

classes.exclusionBoundary: Being assigned to the incident is not qualifying contact.
classes.label: Handling human remains
classes.requiredCorroboration: Documented recovery or handling, or repeated and extreme duty related contact.

classes.exclusionBoundary: Never infer a relationship, and never put a victim or member name or relationship in a shared record.
classes.label: A victim the member knew
classes.requiredCorroboration: A voluntary private confirmation by the member, and nothing else.
classes.withoutTermsBecause: Private only. Searching for relationship language would infer the relationship the library forbids inferring. Reaches a record only by voluntary private confirmation.

classes.exclusionBoundary: No validated threshold exists, and no synthetic incident is created to stand for a pattern.
classes.label: Repeated exposure across many incidents
classes.requiredCorroboration: A pattern across incidents, which no single incident can show.
classes.withoutTermsBecause: Repetition across incidents, which one narrative cannot show. The library carries no validated threshold and forbids creating a synthetic incident to represent a pattern.
